| proven | **Global hashed site field (replaces patches and the tile library)** | Terrain generation | One jittered site per lattice index, placed by hash(seed, i, j); cell polygons use canonical circumcentres so neighbours agree to the bit. The earlier idea of pre-computed patches and a socket-matched tile library was discarded: on-demand generation costs about 2.5 ms per sector, so nothing needs storing. | [live](https://techdevgroup.github.io/boundless-lab/terrain/tile-library)<br>test: test/terrain-world.test.js: flush: every cell edge on a sector border appears with the same vertices in the neighbouring sector |
| proven | **Amorphous sectors by weighted L1 seeds** | Terrain generation | A cell joins the sector of its nearest additively weighted seed (L1 on the lattice, jitter 1, weight 2), so sectors are irregular 4-connected unions of cells and every neighbour in the coarse graph truly touches. Regions repeat the rule on sector indices. Sectors are still blocky near-squares: the connectivity guarantee limits the amorphousness. | [live](https://techdevgroup.github.io/boundless-lab/terrain/assembly)<br>test: test/terrain-world.test.js: sectors are 4-connected unions of cells and neighbours in the coarse graph really touch |

| proven | **Scan waves over the cell graph** | Mechanics | A ping or sweep spreads outward cell by cell, confined by solid walls, building and then exhausting over time. The outgoing pulse is the visible wave: a continuous front with eased per-cell attack and decay, solved once into typed arrays in small time slices off the render loop. Active pings are loud and sharp, passive ones quiet and stale. | [live](https://techdevgroup.github.io/boundless-lab/systems/scan-waves)<br>test: test/scan.test.js: waves never enter solid cells and are confined to the connected open region; arrival = path distance / speed |
| proven | **Echo returns from identifiers** | Mechanics | Anything that identifies itself (you, devices, decoys, adversaries) becomes a new origin when the ping reaches it, and a second geodesic wave spreads out of it, invisibly. It is latched once against the cell you stand in when it reaches you, and then you see that echo field replayed in reverse, in its own hue: a front that starts on the ring through you and contracts onto the source, then a stale glimpse of where it was. One flag, echo.reveal on-arrival or live. | [live](https://techdevgroup.github.io/boundless-lab/systems/scan-waves)<br>test: test/scan-echo.test.js: the reversed front contracts monotonically from the receiver isochrone and ends at the source |
| proven | **Masked stealth fields** | Mechanics | A cast field that absorbs, scrambles or spoofs any scan crossing it, giving cover with a cost, a duration and a tell.
